raffle.title: Prize draws
raffle.heroBody: DeHub prize draws hand out DeHub tokens, hardware and collectibles to the people already using the platform. Entries are earned by taking part, the entry list is published before the draw runs, and the winner is picked by a transaction anyone can read.
raffle.findLiveDraw: Find the live draw in your feed
raffle.noPurchase: No purchase is necessary. Every draw carries a free entry route, and where a ticket is offered it is never the only way in.
raffle.anatomyPrizeBody: Stated when the draw opens. Never changed afterwards.
raffle.anatomyRoutesBody: Listed in full, with the weight each one carries.
raffle.anatomyClosingBody: A fixed timestamp, not "when we get round to it".
raffle.anatomySnapshotBody: Published before the draw is run.
raffle.anatomyRandomnessBody: Drawn on-chain, in a transaction you can open.
raffle.howBody: Four steps, in the same order, every time. The parts that decide who wins happen in public.
raffle.step1Body: Every draw opens with its prize, its closing time and the exact ways to earn an entry, posted in the app and pinned to the feed.
raffle.step2Body: Entries are earned by doing things you already do on DeHub. The announcement lists which actions count for that draw and how many entries each is worth.
raffle.step3Body: At the closing time the entry list is snapshotted and the winning index is drawn from an on-chain source of randomness, not from a spreadsheet.
raffle.step4Body: The snapshot, the transaction and the winning entry all go up together, so anyone can re-check the result rather than take our word for it.
raffle.entriesBody: Draws are weighted towards people who use DeHub. Each announcement names the routes that count for it. These are the ones draws are usually built from.
raffle.postBody: Original posts, videos and comments count towards draws that name them.
raffle.stakeBody: An open staking position earns entries for the draws that weight it.
raffle.arcadeBody: Arcade sessions and leaderboard placings feed draws built around games.
raffle.stagesBody: Turning up to live audio stages counts, whether you speak or listen.
raffle.ticketBody: Some draws also sell a ticket paid in DeHub tokens. Where they do, the price and the per-wallet cap are published up front.
raffle.collectibleBody: Selected NFT collections carry standing entries into draws that name them.
raffle.fairnessTitle: Why the result can be trusted
raffle.fairnessBody: A raffle is only worth entering if the operator cannot quietly pick the winner. Three things make that true here.
raffle.fair1Body: The entry list is snapshotted at the stated closing time and published before the draw runs. Nothing can be added to it afterwards, including by us.
raffle.fair2Body: The winning index is derived on-chain, so the number that decides the draw exists in a public transaction rather than in an internal tool.
raffle.fair3Body: Snapshot, transaction hash and winning entry are published as one set. Re-running the arithmetic from public data has to reach the same winner.
raffle.neverPayTitle: DeHub will never ask you to pay to release a prize
raffle.neverPayBody: Winners are named in the app and in the public result post. Nobody from DeHub will contact you for a fee, a seed phrase, a private key or a wallet signature to hand over a prize. Any message that does is an impersonation. Report it and delete it.
raffle.faqBody: The ones we get asked most often about draws, entries and prizes.
raffle.faq1Q: Do I have to buy anything to enter a DeHub prize draw?
raffle.faqPurchaseAnswer: No. Every draw carries at least one free entry route, earned by taking part on DeHub. Some draws additionally sell a ticket paid in DeHub tokens, but a ticket is never the only way in.
raffle.faq2Q: How do I know the draw was not fixed?
raffle.faq2A: The entry list is snapshotted and published before the draw runs, and the winning index is drawn from an on-chain source of randomness. The snapshot, the transaction and the winning entry are published together so the result can be recomputed by anyone.
raffle.faq3A: Winners are notified in the app and named in the result post. There is no email asking for a payment, a seed phrase or a wallet signature. DeHub will never ask for any of those to release a prize.
raffle.faq4Q: How long do I have to claim?
raffle.faq4A: Fourteen days from the result being published. Token prizes settle to the winner's DeHub wallet on Base. Physical prizes are arranged directly with the team, and shipping is covered where we can legally ship.
raffle.faq5A: Anyone with a DeHub account who is over 18 and lives somewhere the draw is lawful. DeHub staff, contractors and their households are not eligible, and draws are void where local law prohibits them.
raffle.faq6A: There is no fixed schedule. Draws are tied to launches, milestones and partner campaigns, and each is announced in the app when it opens.
raffle.ctaBody: Whatever is live now is announced in your feed. Turn on notifications so the next one does not pass you by.
raffle.legal: Prize draws are promotional and open to DeHub account holders aged 18 or over, void where local law prohibits them. DeHub staff, contractors and their households are not eligible. Prizes are not exchangeable for cash unless stated, and each draw's own announcement carries its full terms.

commonGround.step1Placeholder: The best case they could make is that…
commonGround.step2Title: What do you and they actually agree on?
commonGround.reminderBody: Most disagreements are not a choice between two extremes. When a question feels like either-or, there is usually a third option somewhere in the middle.
commonGround.example1: A neighbour who wants a quieter street and a neighbour who wants more parking can both be right about what they need.
commonGround.example2: Two parents can disagree about screen time and still agree that the child should sleep well and do fine at school.

brief.title: Write a clear visual brief
brief.body1: Describe a concrete subject, its action and the setting. Add framing or camera movement when it helps the scene. Keep unrelated ideas for another draft.
brief.body2: Lighting, lens and style directions guide the model. They do not guarantee physical camera behavior or an exact image. Change one part at a time so you can compare revisions.
brief.body3: Before generating, review the selected model, supported attachments, dimensions and price. Keep the original draft so you can return to it.
brief.question: Which brief is easiest to revise?
brief.answer0: A clear subject, action and setting
brief.exercise: A ceramic teapot on a wooden table beside a window. Soft morning light, medium framing, simple background. Keep the teapot as the clear subject.

continuity.title: Plan shots and review continuity
continuity.body1: Use the Film panel in the editor to save a brief and ordered shots. Prepare each frame or clip separately, review its quote, and select an accepted result.
continuity.body2: Attach only references accepted by your chosen model. Reusing a reference can guide appearance; it does not train an identity or guarantee a match. Characters and voices can vary between generations.
continuity.body3: Keep successful takes and assemble them in the timeline. Review motion, faces, dialogue and transitions before export.
continuity.question: What supports continuity across shots?
continuity.answer1: Approved references and reviewed shot notes
continuity.exercise: Wide shot of a lone traveler reaching a quiet coast at sunrise. Slow forward camera movement, calm atmosphere. One continuous shot.

campaign.title: Use approved product facts
campaign.body1: Start with product facts you can verify. Review imported metadata before using it. Write the headline and call to action explicitly; do not invent prices, reviews or performance claims.

getting-started.title: Getting Started
getting-started.intro: There are five ways into DeHub and none of them need you to already own a wallet: Google, Apple, a code sent to your email, a code sent by SMS, or an existing wallet you connect. Everything except the wallet route creates a non-custodial wallet for you in the background — you hold the keys, and DeHub sponsors the gas so you can post, tip and collect without ever buying a native token.

steps.1: Visit dehub.io — the home feed is the front page, so you can look around before signing in.
steps.2: Click 'Sign In'. You'll see Google and Apple, fields for an email address or a phone number, and 'Connect Wallet' for an existing one.
steps.3: With Google or Apple, complete the provider's flow. With email or SMS, enter the code that arrives.
steps.4: A wallet is created and secured for you on first sign-in. Connecting your own wallet instead means one signature to prove the address.
steps.5: Pick a username. It is what people see and it doubles as your dehub.io/<username> profile link.
steps.6: You're in. Explore the feed, set up your profile, and start posting.

tips.1: Social, email and SMS sign-ins never pay gas — DeHub sponsors it. Connected wallets pay their own ETH or BNB.
tips.2: Coming back to a legacy DeHub account? Sign in with the email or phone number it used and the migration finds it for you.
tips.3: You can keep several accounts on one device and switch between them in Settings → Profile.

home-feed.title: Home Feed
home-feed.intro: The home feed is where you see posts from people you follow and trending content. It supports multiple content-type tabs and sorting options.

steps.1: Navigate to /app — this is your home feed.
steps.2: Use the top tabs to filter by content type: Home (all), Videos, Images, Shorts, Music, or Live streams.
steps.3: Swipe left/right on the tabs to see more options on mobile.
steps.4: Use the filter/sort button (top-right of the feed) to change sorting: Hot, New, or Top.
steps.5: Pull down to refresh the feed on mobile.
steps.6: Scroll down to load more posts automatically (infinite scroll).
steps.7: Toggle between Grid and Feed view using the layout switcher.

tips.1: Grid view is great for browsing images quickly.
tips.2: The 'Home' tab shows all content types mixed together.
tips.3: Live tab shows currently active live streams.

creating-posts.title: Creating Posts
creating-posts.intro: Create text posts, share images, videos, voice notes, GIFs, and more. Use hashtags, cashtags, and mentions to increase reach.

steps.1: Click the 'Post' button in the sidebar (desktop) or the + button (mobile).
steps.2: Type your text in the compose area.
steps.3: To add an image or video, click the media icon and select a file.
steps.4: To record a voice note, click the microphone icon.
steps.5: To add a GIF, click the GIF icon and search for one.
steps.6: Use #hashtags to categorize your post (e.g., #crypto, #defi).
steps.9: Click 'Post' to publish. Your post appears in the feed immediately.

tips.1: Posts support markdown-style formatting.
tips.2: You can quote-post by clicking the repost icon on any post and selecting 'Quote'.
tips.3: Categories (hashtags) appear in the 'Talk of the Town' leaderboard.

interacting-with-posts.title: Interacting with Posts
interacting-with-posts.intro: Engage with content by voting, commenting, tipping, bookmarking, sharing, and translating.

steps.1: Upvote or downvote a post using the arrow icons on the left side of any post.
steps.2: Click the comment icon to open the comment section and leave a reply.
steps.3: Click the gem/tip icon to send a tip in DeHub tokens to the post creator.
steps.4: Click the bookmark icon to save a post for later.
steps.5: Click the share icon to copy the post link or share externally.
steps.6: Click the translate button (globe icon) on any post to translate text to your language.
steps.7: For image posts, use the 'Translate Image' button to get an AI-translated version of text within the image.
steps.8: Click on any post to open it in full-screen single-post view.

tips.1: Tips go directly to the creator's wallet in DeHub tokens.
tips.2: You can set a tip amount via quick-select buttons or enter a custom amount.
tips.3: Bookmarked posts are accessible from the Bookmarks page in the sidebar.

explore-search.title: Explore & Search
explore-search.intro: Discover new content and users through the explore page and powerful search functionality.

steps.1: Navigate to /app/explore from the sidebar.
steps.2: Use the search bar at the top to search for users, posts, or content.
steps.3: Filter results by tab: All, People, Posts, Images, Videos, Music, Live.
steps.4: Browse trending topics and categories on the explore page.
steps.5: Click on a trending topic to see all related posts.
steps.6: Click on a user in search results to visit their profile.

tips.1: Search supports usernames, wallet addresses, and content keywords.
tips.2: Trending topics update based on recent posting activity.

profile.title: Profile
profile.intro: Your profile showcases your posts, followers, following, and wallet information.

steps.1: Click your avatar or 'Profile' in the sidebar to view your profile.
steps.2: Click 'Edit Profile' to update your display name, bio, and avatar.
steps.3: Upload a profile picture by clicking on your avatar in edit mode.
steps.4: View your follower and following counts on your profile page.
steps.5: Browse your own posts, media, and liked content via the profile tabs.
steps.6: Copy your wallet address by clicking the copy icon next to it.
steps.7: Visit other users' profiles by clicking their username or avatar anywhere on the platform.

tips.1: Your username is unique and appears in your profile URL (dehub.io/@username).
tips.2: Privacy settings let you control who can see your follower counts.

messages.title: Messages
messages.intro: Send direct messages to other users on the platform.

steps.1: Click 'Messages' in the sidebar to open the messaging page.
steps.2: Click the compose button to start a new conversation.
steps.3: Search for a user by username to message them.
steps.4: Type your message and press send.
steps.5: View your conversation history in the messages list.
steps.6: Click on a conversation to continue chatting.

tips.1: You'll receive a notification when someone messages you.
tips.2: Creators can lock messages behind a tip requirement.

ai-assistant.title: AI Assistant
ai-assistant.intro: Chat with DeHub's built-in AI assistant for help, information, and creative tasks.

steps.1: Click 'Assistant' in the sidebar to open the AI chat.
steps.2: Type your question or request in the chat input.
steps.3: The AI can help with crypto information, platform questions, and general knowledge.
steps.4: Start a new conversation by clicking the new chat button.
steps.5: View your conversation history in the sidebar of the assistant page.
steps.6: You can attach images for the AI to analyze.

tips.1: The AI remembers context within a conversation.
tips.2: You can ask the AI about DeHub features, crypto terms, or general questions.
tips.3: Previous conversations are saved and accessible anytime.

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.intro: Stay updated with likes, comments, tips, follows, and other activity on your content.

steps.1: Click the bell icon or 'Notifications' in the sidebar.
steps.2: View all notifications in a chronological list.
steps.3: Click on a notification to navigate to the related content.
steps.4: Notifications include: new followers, post votes, comments, tips, and mentions.
steps.5: Unread notifications are highlighted — they mark as read when viewed.

tips.1: The notification badge shows the count of unread notifications.
tips.2: Tip notifications show how many tokens you received.

wallet.title: Wallet
wallet.intro: View your DeHub token balances across multiple chains, check staking deposits, and manage your assets.

steps.1: Click 'Wallet' in the sidebar to open the wallet page.
steps.2: View your total token balance aggregated across all supported chains.
steps.3: See per-chain breakdowns: Ethereum, Base, BNB Chain, and more.
steps.4: Check your staking deposits and rewards.
steps.5: Click 'Refresh Scan' to update your balances from on-chain data.
steps.6: Copy your wallet address to receive tokens from others.

tips.1: Balances update automatically but you can force a refresh anytime.
tips.2: The wallet shows both liquid (available) and staked balances.

staking.title: Staking
staking.intro: Stake your DeHub tokens to earn rewards and increase your governance voting power.

steps.1: Navigate to the 'Staking' page from the sidebar.
steps.2: Enter the number of tokens you want to stake.
steps.3: Select the chain you want to stake on.
steps.4: Confirm the transaction in your wallet (external wallets) or it auto-executes (social login).
steps.5: View your staked amounts and any pending rewards.
steps.6: To unstake, enter the amount and confirm the unstaking transaction.

tips.1: Staking increases your vote weight in governance proposals.
tips.2: Social-login users don't need gas to stake — it's gasless.
tips.3: You can stake on multiple chains simultaneously.

leaderboard.title: Leaderboard
leaderboard.intro: See who's on top! The leaderboard ranks users by balance, daily spending, and trending topics.

steps.1: Navigate to the 'Leaderboard' page from the sidebar.
steps.2: Switch between tabs: Balance, Daily Spent, and Talk of the Town.
steps.3: Balance tab ranks users by their total token holdings.
steps.4: Daily Spent tab shows who's been most active tipping in the last 24 hours.
steps.5: Talk of the Town shows the most-discussed topics/categories.
steps.6: Click on any user to visit their profile.
steps.7: The leaderboard updates periodically throughout the day.

tips.1: Daily rankings reset every 24 hours.
tips.2: Talk of the Town tracks single-word categories from hashtags.

command-centre.title: Command Centre
command-centre.intro: A dashboard overview showing your key metrics and platform activity at a glance.

steps.1: Click 'Command Centre' in the sidebar.
steps.2: View your profile summary, including post count, followers, and engagement.
steps.3: See your recent activity and trending topics.
steps.4: Access quick links to commonly used features.

tips.1: The Command Centre gives you a bird's-eye view of your DeHub presence.

governance.title: Governance
governance.intro: Participate in platform governance by creating proposals and voting on community decisions.

steps.1: Navigate to 'Governance' from the sidebar.
steps.2: Browse active proposals submitted by the community.
steps.3: Click on a proposal to read its full description and discussion.
steps.4: Vote on proposals using the thumbs up/down buttons — your vote weight depends on how many DeHub tokens you have staked.
steps.5: Leave comments on proposals to discuss with the community.
steps.6: Submit your own proposal by clicking the 'Create Proposal' button.

tips.1: Your voting power is determined by the number of tokens you have staked.
tips.2: Badge holders may get additional vote weight.
tips.3: Proposals go through stages: Active → Passed/Rejected.

bookmarks.title: Bookmarks
bookmarks.intro: Save posts to your bookmarks for easy access later.

steps.1: Click the bookmark icon on any post to save it.
steps.2: Navigate to 'Bookmarks' in the sidebar to view all saved posts.
steps.3: Click on a bookmarked post to view it in full.
steps.4: Remove a bookmark by clicking the bookmark icon again.

tips.1: Bookmarks are private — only you can see your saved posts.
tips.2: There's no limit to how many posts you can bookmark.

settings.title: Settings
settings.intro: Customize your DeHub experience with language, privacy, and display preferences.

steps.1: Click 'Settings' in the sidebar.
steps.2: Change your display language from the language selector.
steps.3: Adjust privacy settings: control who sees your follower counts and following list.
steps.4: Set your default post visibility preferences.
steps.5: Manage notification preferences.

tips.1: DeHub supports multiple languages — the entire interface translates.
tips.2: Privacy settings apply immediately.

posting-allowance.title: Your Daily Home Feed Allowance
posting-allowance.intro: Post as much as you like, every day, for free. Your staking badge sets how many text posts and how much video, image and audio reach the public home feed each day. Anything past that still publishes, it just shows on your profile and to your followers instead of the home feed.

steps.1: Post as normal. Nothing is ever charged and nothing is ever blocked.
steps.2: Text posts and media are separate allowances, so a day of uploading video still leaves your text posts for the home feed.
steps.3: Media is one shared pool of data per day across video, images and audio, so lots of small posts all fit.
steps.4: Once you pass either allowance, new posts of that kind go to your profile and your followers' Following feed.
steps.5: Nothing is hidden: everything you post stays on your profile.
steps.6: Both allowances reset at midnight UTC.

tips.1: A higher staking badge puts more of your posts on the home feed each day.
tips.2: Reposts, comments, reactions, tips and messages never touch the allowance.
tips.3: Your followers see every post you make in their Following feed.
tips.4: Each single file still has a size limit set by your badge.

reactions-and-safety.title: Reactions, Muting & Mature Content
reactions-and-safety.intro: There are nine reactions behind the like button, and a set of controls for deciding what you see and who can reach you.

steps.1: Hold the thumbs-up on any post to open the reaction tray: like, love, respect, hot, lol, sad, cry, dislike and poo.
steps.2: The seven positive ones count towards the post's like total; dislike and poo count against it.
steps.3: Your reaction is weighted by your staking badge, so a badge holder's reaction moves the count further than one vote.
steps.4: Tap the X in a post's header to mute its author — they drop out of your feed straight away.
steps.5: Creators mark their own posts as mature while composing them; those posts stay off the public home feed.
steps.6: To see mature posts everywhere, turn on 'Show mature content' in Settings.

tips.1: A mature post is still fully visible on the creator's profile and to the people who follow them.
tips.2: Blocking from a profile goes further than muting and cuts off messaging too.
tips.3: The reaction tray shows who reacted and with what, so you can see the room rather than just a number.

stages.title: Stages (Live Audio Rooms)
stages.intro: Stages are live audio rooms built into DeHub. A host opens a room, brings speakers up, and anyone can drop in to listen from the Stages page or a shared link.

steps.1: Open 'Stages' in the sidebar to see what is live now and what is scheduled.
steps.2: Tap a live stage to join as a listener, or set a reminder on a scheduled one and get told when it starts.
steps.3: Start your own from the same page — you can go live straight from the browser, with no OBS or stream key.
steps.4: As host, bring speakers on stage, mute or remove them, share your screen, and drive the soundboard.
steps.5: Listeners send live reactions and talk in the room chat without coming on stage.
steps.6: Every stage records, and the recording plays back afterwards from the card it appears on.

tips.1: Live subtitles caption each speaker and translate into whatever language you are reading in.
tips.2: Live dubbing can speak the room aloud in the host's own cloned voice, billed by the minute in DeHub tokens.
tips.3: Hosts can put a radio station on air or play their own music clips between conversations.
tips.4: A mini-player keeps the room going in the corner while you browse the rest of the app.

communities.title: Communities & Events
communities.intro: Communities are member-run spaces with their own feed, members and activity. Events add time-bound programming on top of them.

steps.1: Open 'Communities' in the sidebar and browse the public ones.
steps.2: Join in one tap. New activity shows as an unread badge in the navigation.
steps.3: Post, discuss, run polls and tip inside a community's own feed.
steps.4: Community owners moderate their own space and can grant admin rights to others.
steps.5: Open 'Events' for scheduled programming, with a full page per event you can follow along with live.

tips.1: Community chat supports @mentions and @here, so a post can reach the room.
tips.2: An invite link lets you bring people straight into a community.

arcade.title: Arcade
arcade.intro: Five games run inside DeHub in a browser tab — nothing to install, nothing to buy.

steps.1: Open 'Arcade' in the sidebar.
steps.2: Pick a game: King's Gambit (3D chess with an online Elo ladder), Claude of Duty (a shooter that generates its own art as it loads), Jungle Trail (a procedural rainforest walk), Street Slayer (a beat 'em up made for DeHub) or Chartopia (a walkable trading floor).
steps.3: Play in the tab. King's Gambit and Street Slayer keep leaderboards.
steps.4: Chartopia also runs in a VR headset through WebXR.

tips.1: Two of them hide inside the appearance themes — set the app to War for Claude of Duty, or Jungle for Jungle Trail.
tips.2: Every game has its own share card, so a link to one unfurls properly wherever you post it.

bounties-stores.title: Bounties & Stores
bounties-stores.intro: Two ways to turn the platform into income: post or claim a bounty, or open a storefront and sell to your audience.

steps.1: Open 'Bounties' to browse open work, filtered by category or currency.
steps.2: Claim one, do the work, and submit it to collect the reward — anyone can be a hunter, no application needed.
steps.3: Post your own bounty with a brief and a reward in DeHub tokens or USDC. It goes into escrow the moment you post it.
steps.4: Open 'Stores' to set up a storefront with its own page, branding and listings.
steps.5: Products are priced and settled in DeHub tokens through the built-in wallet, with no external checkout.

tips.1: Bounties are organised into Social Media, Clipping and Contracts.
tips.2: A dispute flow settles disagreements over delivery, so escrow always resolves fairly.
tips.3: Creators use bounties to grow a community — shares, clips and reactions are all valid tasks.

creator-studio.title: Creator Studio & Editor
creator-studio.intro: Creator Studio generates images, video, music, voice and 3D models from a prompt, and hands them to an editor — including a full multi-track video editor that runs in the browser.

steps.1: Open Creator Studio and describe what you want made.
steps.2: The server quotes the cost before the job runs, so you see what it costs before you spend it.
steps.3: Renders continue in a shared queue while you carry on browsing the app.
steps.4: Arrange the results in the Canva-style editor, or open the video editor for a real timeline with cutting, layering and export.
steps.5: Drop the finished piece straight into a post, a short or a store listing.

tips.1: A free stock asset library sits alongside the Studio for anything you would rather not generate.
tips.2: Generation is paid for in DeHub tokens from your wallet — you sign one transfer per job, and the price is quoted before you pay.
tips.3: Heavier users can take an Ultra, Team or Scale plan, which sends a monthly token allowance straight to their wallet.

buying-dhb.title: Buying Tokens
buying-dhb.intro: Buy DeHub tokens directly within the app using the built-in swap interface.

steps.1: Navigate to the 'Buy' page from the sidebar.
steps.2: Select the token you want to swap from (e.g., ETH, USDC).
steps.3: Enter the amount you want to spend or the number of tokens you want to receive.
steps.4: Review the exchange rate and estimated output.
steps.5: Click the settings gear icon to adjust slippage tolerance (default is 1%).
steps.6: Confirm the swap transaction.
steps.7: DeHub tokens will appear in your wallet once the transaction completes.

tips.1: Higher slippage tolerance = more likely to execute, but potential for worse pricing.
tips.2: Always check the exchange rate before confirming.
tips.3: You can set custom slippage in the settings panel.

bridge.title: Bridge
bridge.intro: Move your DeHub tokens between supported blockchains using the cross-chain bridge.

steps.1: Navigate to the 'Bridge' page from the sidebar.
steps.2: Select the source chain (where your tokens currently are).
steps.3: Select the destination chain (where you want to send them).
steps.4: Enter the number of tokens to bridge.
steps.5: Review the bridge fee and estimated arrival time.
steps.6: Confirm the bridge transaction.
steps.7: The team sends the tokens out on the destination chain, usually within 1-5 business days.

tips.1: Bridge fees vary by chain pair.
tips.2: Bridge payouts are made by hand for now.
tips.3: Always double-check the destination chain before confirming.

music-tv.title: Music & TV
music-tv.intro: Enjoy media content directly within DeHub — stream music and watch live TV channels.

steps.1: Navigate to 'Music' from the sidebar to browse and play music posts.
steps.2: Navigate to 'TV' to access live TV channels.
steps.3: Browse channels by category or country.
steps.4: Click on a channel to start watching.
steps.5: Use the player controls to adjust volume and playback.
steps.6: Report broken channels using the report button.

tips.1: TV channels are community-verified for reliability.
tips.2: Music posts can be played while browsing other content.

post-info.title: Post Info & Fractions
post-info.intro: A minted post is an NFT split into 1,000 fractions. The Post Info page shows on-chain data, engagement stats, ownership breakdown, and lets you trade fractions of any post — on an unminted post it offers to mint instead.

steps.1: Tap the 'ⓘ' icon on any post to open its Post Info page.
steps.2: At the top you'll see the Token ID (unique on-chain identifier) and the transaction hash — click the hash to view it on the block explorer.
steps.3: Below that, engagement stats show total likes, dislikes, views, comments, and tips received.
steps.4: The Holders section shows a progress bar of how many of the 1,000 fractions the creator still owns, plus a list of all fraction holders with their balances and percentages.
steps.5: If the post is pay-per-view (PPV), you'll see the price, currency, and how many users have purchased access.
steps.6: Post owners can change visibility (Public, Unlisted, or Private) and edit the title/description directly from this page.

tips.1: A freshly minted post starts with the creator holding all 1,000 fractions (100% ownership).
tips.2: The transaction hash links to BaseScan or BscScan depending on the chain.
tips.3: Unlisted posts don't appear in feeds but can still be accessed via direct link.

trading-fractions.title: Trading Fractions
trading-fractions.intro: Fraction trading — browsing listings, making offers, listing your own — lives on the web app at dehub.io, on each post's Post Info page.

steps.1: Open dehub.io in a browser and sign in with the same account.
steps.2: Open the post's Post Info page and switch to its Marketplace tab.
steps.3: Browse listings, make an offer at your price, or list fractions you hold.
steps.4: Once a trade completes, the change shows up in your Fractions tab here on mobile.

tips.1: Owning fractions of a post means you hold a share of that on-chain NFT.
tips.2: Check a post's holders on the web marketplace to see ownership distribution before buying.
tips.3: As a creator, selling fractions lets fans co-own your content.

minting-posts.title: Minting Posts (Creating NFTs)
minting-posts.intro: Minting is optional. A post publishes off-chain the moment you send it — no wallet, no signature, no gas — and you can mint it as an NFT whenever you want, either as you compose it or later from the post itself.

steps.1: Click the 'Post' button in the sidebar (desktop) or the + button (mobile).
steps.2: Write your text, attach media (images, videos, audio), and add categories.
steps.3: Leave 'Mint post' off to publish off-chain, or switch it on to mint as you publish.
steps.4: Publishing never waits on the chain: the post appears in the feed either way.
steps.5: To mint later, open the post's 'ⓘ' info page and use the Mint action there.
steps.6: Once minted, the post gets a Token ID and a transaction hash you can verify on-chain, and you hold all 1,000 fractions of it.

tips.1: Social, email and SMS sign-ins pay zero gas — DeHub sponsors minting fees.
tips.2: External-wallet users need ETH on Base or BNB on BNB Chain for gas.
tips.3: Minting is what makes a post tradeable and royalty-bearing. An unminted post still earns tips and views.
tips.4: The on-chain record is permanent once minted, even if the post is later deleted from the feed.

glossary.title: Glossary
glossary.intro: A comprehensive glossary of crypto and platform terminology to help you navigate Web3.

steps.1: Navigate to 'Glossary' from the sidebar.
steps.2: Browse terms alphabetically or use the search to find specific terms.
steps.3: Click on a term to see its full definition and explanation.
steps.4: Terms cover crypto concepts, DeFi terminology, and DeHub-specific features.

tips.1: Great resource for newcomers to crypto and Web3.
tips.2: The glossary is regularly updated with new terms.

depin.title: DePin
depin.ctaBody: Origin fallback, encrypted protected media and verified work come before public node rewards.
depin.ctaTitle: Launch only when failure is safe.
depin.earlyAccessBody: A lightweight, browser-based node is live below. A heavier, always-on desktop node is a stated future direction, not available yet. Participation never guarantees a reward.
depin.footerNote: DePin participation is a contribution service, not an investment product. Availability, eligibility and rewards may change.
depin.heroBlurb: Contribute spare storage, bandwidth and compute to help host, transcode and deliver DeHub content.
depin.heroCaption: DeHub keeps the origin copy. Community nodes add resilient replicas and local delivery capacity.
depin.heroImageAlt: A compact edge-compute node connected to homes and creator studios
depin.noFixedRate: There is no fixed rate, minimum return, APY or forward estimate. Contribution records are accounting inputs only, not a promise of payment. Any future token settlement would occur on Base and remain subject to eligibility, network rules and applicable law.
depin.nodesLeaveBody: No community machine holds the only copy. Health checks, replicas and origin fallback keep playback available.
depin.nodesLeaveTitle: A network that expects nodes to leave.
depin.privacyBody: Protected media stays encrypted on community hardware. Playback keys are issued separately to authorised viewers.
depin.runningCosts: Running a node uses electricity, internet data and hardware life. Operators may receive nothing, and their costs may exceed any reward.
depin.safestWorkloadBody: DePin supplements DeHub's existing delivery path first. More demanding workloads follow only after verification is proven.
depin.safestWorkloadTitle: Built from the safest workload outward.
depin.threeJobsBody: Operators choose their storage, bandwidth and compute limits. DeHub schedules only the work their machine can safely handle.
depin.transcodeBody: Eligible machines turn uploaded video into adaptive renditions. Every output is checked before it can be served.
depin.transcodeImageAlt: A home creator workstation contributing spare GPU compute
depin.verifiedWorkBody: Contribution is measured through signed receipts, health checks and output validation. Storage alone does not create a reward.
depin.verifiedWorkTitle: Useful work is verified. Rewards stay variable.
depin.hostBody: Nodes keep encrypted or content-addressed segments in a capped local cache. DeHub origin storage remains the source of truth.
depin.deliverBody: Nearby peers share video segments while the normal delivery path stays ready as an automatic fallback.
depin.originBody: Permanent source copy and fallback delivery
depin.availableReplicasBody: Serve verified segments close to demand
depin.offlineNodeBody: Removed from routing until it reconnects
depin.viewerBody: Uses a peer when available, origin when needed
depin.protectedContentBody: Subscriber, private and pay-per-view segments can be stored as ciphertext. Node operators do not receive entitlement keys simply because they host data.
depin.publicContentBody: Encryption prevents casual inspection of cached files, but public media remains watchable through the public DeHub player. We will not claim otherwise.
depin.operatorControlsBody: Operators choose disk limits, bandwidth limits, working hours and eligible public content categories. Removal notices trigger cache purges.
depin.deliveryReceiptsBody: Verified bytes served to real playback sessions.
depin.availabilityBody: Successful retrieval checks and reliable service when assigned.
depin.validOutputBody: Transcodes must pass technical and sampled quality checks.
depin.revenuePoolBody: If activated, a reward budget would be set from platform revenue after the epoch closes.
depin.deliveryBody: Peer-assisted live and video delivery with automatic fallback.
depin.adaptiveVideoBody: Multiple renditions for reliable playback across connection speeds.
depin.desktopNodesBody: Capped storage, bandwidth controls and verified availability.
depin.baseSettlementBody: Revenue-funded claims only after operational and legal review.
depin.faqOfflineQ: What happens when a hosting node goes offline?
depin.faqOfflineA: The coordinator removes it from active routing. Another replica serves the segment, or playback falls back to DeHub origin storage while replacement copies are scheduled.
depin.faqCanOperatorSeeQ: Can a node operator see the content they host?
depin.faqCanOperatorSeeA: Protected content is stored as encrypted segments and the host does not receive playback keys. Public content remains publicly viewable through DeHub by design.
depin.faqHowMuchQ: How much will a node operator receive?
depin.faqHowMuchA: There is no fixed rate or forecast. Verified contribution may receive a share of a revenue-funded reward pool after an epoch closes. Rewards are not guaranteed, and electricity, bandwidth and hardware costs may exceed any reward.
depin.faqSoftwareAvailableQ: Is the node software available now?
depin.faqSoftwareAvailableA: A lightweight, browser-based tier is available today: sign in and opt in on this page, and your open tab becomes a node while it stays open. A heavier, always-on desktop node is a stated future direction — it does not exist yet.
depin.faqInstallNeededQ: Do I need to install anything for the browser node?
depin.faqInstallNeededA: No. It runs entirely in the tab using your browser's local storage. Closing the tab stops your node; there is no background service and no install.
depin.appSignInBlurb: Sign in to see your node ledger: what you have stored, what was verified and what you earned this period.
depin.appNodeBody: The node runs in a browser tab, not in this app. Open DePin on the web, sign in with this account and opt in. Your ledger shows up here.

connect.title: Connect DeHub to your AI assistant
connect.subtitle: Give ChatGPT or Claude access to DeHub — browsing posts, reading comment threads, searching and looking up profiles — by pasting the URL below into your assistant's connector settings.
connect.agentTitle: Want it to post, vote and reply?
connect.agentBody: The URL above is read-only. Create an agent and you get your own connector URL with the key built in — same setup steps, but the assistant can then post, comment, vote and follow as your agent.
connect.chatgptDevMode: Enable Developer mode in the connector settings (read the risk notice shown there).
connect.chatgptComposer: In the chat composer's "+" menu, turn on Developer mode.
connect.chatgptAddSources: Choose Add sources, then Connect more.
connect.nameAndPaste: Name the connector "DeHub" and paste the MCP URL above.
connect.askToUse: Ask {{app}} to use DeHub — for example, "Show me trending posts on DeHub."
connect.claudeEnable: Enable the connector from Claude's chat composer, then ask it to use DeHub.
connect.otherClients: Any other MCP-compatible client works the same way — add a custom MCP server and paste the URL above.
connect.guideIntro: DeHub is available as a native {{app}} connector. Turn it on once and ask {{app}} about DeHub posts, creators and trends — right from the chat.
connect.step1Body: Tap the button above. {{app}} opens straight on the DeHub connector in Settings → Connectors.
connect.step2Body: Turn DeHub on and approve access. {{app}} can then read public DeHub posts, profiles and trending topics.
connect.step3Title: Start a new chat and use it
connect.step3Body: Open a new chat and mention DeHub in your prompt — {{app}} calls the connector automatically.
connect.prompt1: Summarise the top 10 trending posts on DeHub right now.
connect.prompt2: Find posts on DeHub about Bitcoin from the last 24 hours and give me a digest.
connect.prompt3: Look up the DeHub profile @satoshi and tell me what they've posted this week.
connect.faqFreeQ: Is DeHub free to use inside {{app}}?
connect.faqFreeA: Yes. The connector is free to add. Your {{app}} plan needs to support connectors.
connect.faqWhatQ: What can the DeHub connector do?
connect.faqWhatA: Through MCP it can browse public DeHub posts, search topics and look up creator profiles. It does not post on your behalf.
connect.faqAccountQ: Do I need a DeHub account?
connect.chatgptFaqAccount: No account is required to read public content through the connector. A DeHub account is only needed if you want to post, tip or hold DeHub tokens.
connect.claudeFaqAccount: No. Reading public content works without an account. You only need a DeHub account to post, tip or hold DeHub tokens.
